instructions.question: What emotional attitude does the poster of this Swedish tweet clearly express: positive, neutral, or negative?
instructions.rule: Label positive or negative only when the poster's own feeling is evident from emotional words, emoji, exclamations or sarcasm. Otherwise choose neutral. News headlines and retweeted reports stay neutral even when the topic is grim (disease, war, layoffs), unless the poster adds a reaction. Political arguments, campaign lines, calm disagreement, polite agreement, small talk, questions and automatic posts ('Jag gillade ett videoklipp') are neutral. Sarcastic or ironic praise is negative.

neutral.what: Information, news headlines (including bad news shared without comment), political statements and arguments, questions, plans, mild replies, agreement and calm disagreement.
examples: RT @ExpressenRSS: Ebola-utbrottet är det värsta någonsin http://t.co/iNJ6931SJx (The Ebola outbreak is the worst ever)
@CarlssonJhannes Absolut. Jag förstår den ståndpunkten och respekterar den med. (Absolutely. I understand that position and respect it too.)

Högre lärartäthet, av utbildade lärare idag. Det krävs för att bryta det långvariga kunskapstappet! #Alliansen #svpol #jobbvalet (More trained teachers per pupil today. That is needed to break the long knowledge decline!)
@powerpuff_ronja vad ska du läsa? (what are you going to study?)
neutral.cues: links, RT of headlines, #svpol, priser (prices), vad/hur/när (what/how/when), Jag gillade ett videoklipp (I liked a video), times and numbers
neutral.not_for: A headline plus the poster's own reaction, such as 'Sorgligt.' (Sad.) or ':(', is negative. A headline plus 'Bra att...' (Good that...) is positive.

positive.what: Clear joy, praise, enthusiasm, love, congratulations, gratitude, excitement, or explicit approval of something or someone.
examples: @papperferdinand grattis till ert giftemål det var ett vackert bröllop :,) (congrats on your marriage, it was a beautiful wedding)
RT @BenjaminDousa: 'Vi har stått upp för våra frihetsideal. Vi har öppnat upp för arbetskraftsinvandring.' Reinfeldt. Är. Så. Bra. #dinröst (Reinfeldt. Is. So. Good.)
@stroemberg en av de bästa burgarna i stan så ja på den! (one of the best burgers in town so yes to it!)
positive.cues: grattis (congrats), härligt (lovely), älskar (love), underbart (wonderful), så bra (so good), tack (thanks), <3, :D, pepp (excited)
positive.not_for: Polite agreement or a friendly greeting with no real excitement is neutral. Praise that is clearly ironic is negative.

negative.what: Clear anger, sadness, frustration, complaints, insults, mockery, sarcasm or ironic jabs at people, parties or situations.
examples: Livet e hårt och sen dör man (Life is hard and then you die)

RT @fredrik_t_k: Tur att bara tre av fyra laddplatser i Vällingbygaraget var upptagna av fossilbilar... #elbil #swegreen http://t.co/naXqX0… (Lucky that only three of four charging spots were taken by fossil cars...)
@FrHaJo Det missade jag: 'Jag heter Thomas Bodström. Ödmjukhet är mitt mellannamn.' (My name is Thomas Bodström. Humility is my middle name.)
negative.cues: hatar (hate), jävla/fan (damn), sorgligt (sad), jobbigt (annoying), tråkigt (boring), :(, 😭, ironic 'tur att' (lucky that), mocking quotes
negative.not_for: Swearing used for enthusiasm ('SÅ. JÄVLA. BRA', SO. DAMN. GOOD) is positive. Grim news with no reaction from the poster and sober policy criticism are neutral.
